**Construction:** A dry cell (Leclanché cell) consists of a cylindrical zinc container that acts as the anode (-). Inside is a central graphite rod acting as the cathode (+), surrounded by a moist paste of $\text{MnO}_2$, $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$, and $\text{ZnCl}_2$ packed in a porous paper lining.

**Working / Cell Reactions:**
* **Anode (Oxidation):** 
  $$\text{Zn}_{(s)} \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}_{(aq)} + 2e^{-}$$
* **Cathode (Reduction):** 
  $$2\text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{NH}_4^+ + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Mn}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Ammonia produced complexes with $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ to prevent gas pressure build-up. It yields a potential of roughly $1.5\text{ V}$.
proTip: Clearly write both anode and cathode half-cell reactions as they carry major marks in evaluation.
